dedupe_keys.name: nigeria flood impact data nema on hdx and the nema flood dashboard 2024

description: OCHA Nigeria publishes on the Humanitarian Data Exchange a dataset of flood-affected people and locations in Nigeria, sourced from the National Emergency Management Agency and State Emergency Management Agencies. It holds nine resources covering January 2022 to September 2025: counts of affected people in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe for 2024 and for September 2024 to September 2025, national figures for 2023 and for 2022, and flood-affected areas in 2022 by local government area and by ward as CSV and as p-coded shapefiles, under a CC BY licence, with a yearly update frequency and a last change on 24 October 2025. NEMA's own Flood Dashboard 2024 gathers the flood outlook, situation reports, a risk prediction map of local government areas at high and medium risk for October and November 2024, daily flood water levels downstream of the Benue and Niger confluence at Lokoja, and state figures; for Borno it reports 414,176 people affected, 389,267 displaced, 37 deaths and 7,155 houses damaged after inflows overtopped the Alau Dam and a section collapsed. Access is free. Caveats: the HDX methodology is marked as direct observational and anecdotal data, and the resources use different areas and periods. Coverage is Nigeria. It supports historical event analysis and hazard exposure studies of dams, roads and housing; related records are the GRID3 Nigeria facility datasets on HDX and DesInventar Sri Lanka.
